caption: Sequencer: four timed phases started by each beat - each its own colour, its brightness its progress
why: Some effects are routines: a burst, a spin, a hold, a rest. Sequencer runs a cycle of up to four phases, each lasting the time you give it, started by a trigger or straight away, and tells you which phase is on and how far through it is.

Drive different parts of the effect from which phase it is, and their speed from the progress. Its neighbours: Steps plays a value per trigger; Counter counts triggers; Scenes fades between looks; Sequencer is timed phases.
steps: **Audio**'s `beat` is the **trigger**: each kick starts the cycle again.

**phase 1** is 0.15 seconds, **phase 2** 0.3, **phase 3** 0.15 and **phase 4** 0.6. **loop** is off, so after phase 4 it stops until the next trigger; **run at start** is on, so it starts once when the effect does.
`phase` (1..4 while running, 0 when finished) times 0.25 is the **Palette**'s index - each phase its colour; `progress` (0..1 through the phase) is the brightness, so each phase ramps up.
`since` is the seconds since the cycle began and `running` whether it is. The trace shows the phase stepping 1, 2, 3, 4 after each kick.

try.label: Loop
try.text: loop on: when phase 4 ends it starts again at phase 1 by itself, between beats too.

try.label: Long first phase
try.text: phase 1 at 0.8: the first phase takes most of the gap between kicks.
